key_idea: Two friends meet after d_manhattan/(v_i+v_j); maximising a ratio over pairs is done by parametric search where the test max(d_ij - t(v_i+v_j)) >= 0 separates per point after rotating to u=x+y and u=x-y.
sketch: The meeting time of a pair is Manhattan distance over the sum of speeds, since both can walk towards each other along a shortest grid path. For a guess t, d_ij - t(v_i+v_j) >= 0 for some pair iff for one of the two diagonal directions max_i(u_i - t v_i) + max_j(-u_j - t v_j) >= 0, an O(N) scan. I use Dinkelbach iteration instead of bisection: take the argmax pair for the current t, set t to that pair's exact ratio (kept as an integer fraction, compared with __int128), and stop when it no longer improves; it converges in a handful of rounds. Pitfalls: if the two argmaxes are the same point skip that direction (the value is negative for t>0 anyway), all points coincident gives 0, and printing needs enough digits for relative 1e-6. Stress-tested against the O(N^2) exact brute force.
